title: Annotate Gene Function with Uproc
author: James E Thornton Jr
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kt8cwrw
materials: Move into your anvio-genes directory. $ cd /rsgrps/bh_class/username/anvio-genes
Move into the function directory. $ cd function
Move into your function directory. $ cd /rsgrps/bh_class/username/anvio-genes/function

steps.title: Log into HPC
steps.instruction: Connect to the high‑performance cluster with ssh, e.g. `ssh hpc` then `ssh ocelote` (replace with your host name).

steps.title: Create uproc_function.sh script
steps.instruction:
Create a file named `uproc_function.sh` with the following content (preserve line breaks). Edit the `FASTA` variable to point to your gene‑call file (e.g. `/rsgrps/bh_class/username/anvio-genes/nucleotides.fna` or `.faa`). Replace `netid` in the `#PBS -M` line with your email address.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#PBS -W group_list=bh_class
#PBS -q windfall
#PBS -l select=1:ncpus=12:mem=23gb
#PBS -l pvmem=22gb
#PBS -l walltime=24:00:00
#PBS -l cput=24:00:00
#PBS -M netid@email.arizona.edu   # replace netid
#PBS -m bea

#--------------EDIT THESE---------------
FASTA="/rsgrps/bh_class/username/anvio-genes/nucleotides.fna"   # change if needed
OUT_DIR="/rsgrps/bh_class/username/anvio-genes/function"
OUTPUT="$OUT_DIR/uproc-out"
#---------------------------------------
export UPROC="/rsgrps/bh_class/bin/uproc-dna"
export DATA="/rsgrps/bh_class/data/uproc"
export UPROC_MODEL="$DATA/model"
export UPROC_OUT_DIR="$OUT_DIR/uproc-out"
export PFAM="$DATA/pfam27ready"
export KEGG="$DATA/keggready"

$UPROC --preds --short --threads 12 --output $OUTPUT.pfam $PFAM $UPROC_MODEL $FASTA
$UPROC --preds --short --threads 12 --output $OUTPUT.kegg $KEGG $UPROC_MODEL $FASTA
```
Make sure to replace the placeholder `netid` and adjust the `FASTA` path as needed.

steps.title: Create log directories
steps.instruction: Make directories for standard output and error files: `mkdir std-out std-err`.

steps.title: Submit uproc job
steps.instruction: Submit the script to the scheduler, directing output and error to the directories you just created: `qsub -e std-err -o std-out uproc_function.sh`.

steps.title: Create format-anvio.pl script
steps.instruction: Create a Perl script named `format-anvio.pl` containing the code provided (starts with `#!/usr/bin/env perl` and includes `use strict;`). The script parses a uproc output file, looks up functional descriptions, and writes a tab‑separated file with columns `gene_callers_id`, `source`, `accession`, `function`, `e_value`.

steps.title: Convert uproc output to Anvi'o format
steps.instruction:
Make the Perl script executable and run it for both KEGG and PFAM results, then combine the files while removing duplicate header lines.

```bash
chmod 755 format-anvio.pl
# KEGG conversion
./format-anvio.pl uproc-out.kegg /rsgrps/bh_class/kegg_to_desc uproc-kegg-anvio kegg > input_matrix.txt
# PFAM conversion (append without header)
./format-anvio.pl uproc-out.pfam /rsgrps/bh_class/pfam_to_domain uproc-pfam-anvio pfam | egrep -v "gene_callers_id" >> input_matrix.txt
```
(Equivalent one‑liner shown in the original text also works.)

steps.title: Check job status
steps.instruction: Monitor the PBS job until it finishes successfully: `qstat -u username`. Proceed only after the job is complete.

steps.title: Download functional matrix
steps.instruction:
From a local terminal (outside the HPC), copy the matrix file to the directory containing your Anvi'o contigs database:

```bash
scp netid@sftp.hpc.arizona.edu:/rsgrps/bh_class/username/anvio-genes/function/input_matrix.txt .
```

steps.title: Download taxonomy files
steps.instruction:
Copy the centrifuge taxonomy reports and hits to the same local directory:

```bash
scp netid@sftp.hpc.arizona.edu:/rsgrps/bh_class/username/anvio-genes/taxonomy/*centrifuge_report.tsv .
scp netid@sftp.hpc.arizona.edu:/rsgrps/bh_class/username/anvio-genes/taxonomy/*centrifuge_hits.tsv .
```

steps.title: Import taxonomy into Anvi'o
steps.instruction:
In an Anvi'o terminal, run:

```bash
anvi-import-taxonomy -c contigs.db -i centrifuge_report.tsv centrifuge_hits.tsv -p centrifuge
```
Make sure you are in the directory that contains `contigs.db` and the downloaded taxonomy files.

steps.title: Launch Anvi'o (Docker)
steps.instruction:
If you are using the Docker image, start Anvi'o with:

```bash
docker run --rm -v ~/path/to/files:/my_data -p 8080:8080 -it meren/anvio:latest
```

steps.title: Import functional matrix into Anvi'o
steps.instruction:
From the Anvi'o terminal, import the functional annotations:

```bash
anvi-import-functions -c contigs.db -i input_matrix.txt
```
